title: Connectome simulations identify a central pattern generator circuit for fly walking
source_locator: bioRxiv v1 Fig. 2h-k (v2/PMC13142387 Fig. 2h-j, Extended Data Fig. 3); Methods (optogenetic activation); Supplementary Video 1
quote: At higher optogenetic stimulus intensities, flies walked with higher forward velocity (mean ± 95% c.i., n=7 flies, 8 trials per fly).
mapping_basis: The paper uses the MANC type name DNg100 (formerly BDN2), which type_list.csv lists as exactly one MANC type.
stimulation: 638 nm laser focused on front left leg body-coxa joint, 1200 Hz 30% duty cycle; 0.03, 0.09, 0.33 mW/mm2 (strongest 0.33); 5 s on per 15 s trial
sensory_condition: decapitated, tethered on air-supported spherical treadmill
frequency_note: Left front leg stepping frequency increased with laser intensity (Fig. 2j); numeric values not read in text.
notes: Paper text: DNg100 activation initiates forward walking in headless flies; forward velocity (FicTrac) and stepping frequency rose with intensity. Specificity of the line was not described in the text I read. Simulation results for DNg100 were visible in a web-search summary (see notes.md).

title: Connectome simulations identify a central pattern generator circuit for fly walking
source_locator: bioRxiv v1 Fig. 4c-e (v2/PMC13142387 Fig. 5c-e); Supplementary Video 2
quote: Activating DNb08 produced oscillatory movement of the front and middle legs (n=10 flies, 8 stim-on and 4 stim-off trials per fly).
mapping_basis: The paper uses the MANC type name DNb08, which type_list.csv lists as one MANC type; driver_lines.csv also maps SS70620 to DNb08 only.
stimulation: 638 nm laser focused on front left leg body-coxa joint, 1200 Hz 30% duty cycle; intensity for DNb08 not stated; 8 stim-on and 4 stim-off trials per fly
sensory_condition: decapitated, tethered; text says movements were evoked more reliably with the spherical treadmill removed
coordination_notes: Rhythmic leg movements resembling searching movements of unloaded legs, not coordinated walking.
notes: headless_surface set to other because the text does not say whether the quantified trials were on the ball or with the ball removed. The paper shows only a VNC expression image (Fig. 5c legend) and does not state the line's specificity. saw_simulation_score is set true to be conservative: a page summary said simulation results exist for DNb08 in this paper, although I did not read a score.

title: Central versus peripheral neural control of a coordinated walking pattern in Drosophila
source_locator: bioRxiv v2 Fig. 1b-e (ball condition), Extended Data Fig. 1c
quote: In case of DNg100 stimulation, all six legs show rhythmic forward-stepping across all four conditions
mapping_basis: The paper uses the MANC type name DNg100 (BDN2), which type_list.csv lists as exactly one MANC type.
stimulation: 625 nm, 66 Hz, ~0.040 mW/mm2; 3 s light after 2 s off per trial
n_flies_note: 60-70 trials across 6-7 flies per genotype and condition
notes: Forward velocity measured on the ball (Fig. 1b); DNg100 flies reach only ~0-8 mm/s. Authors call the split-GAL4 lines 'highly specific'. saw_simulation_score is true because DNg100 simulation results were visible in a web-search summary of Pugliese et al.

title: Central versus peripheral neural control of a coordinated walking pattern in Drosophila
quote: DNg97 stimulation drove stepping rhythms across all six legs in the ball-condition.
mapping_basis: The paper uses the MANC type name DNg97 (oDN1), which type_list.csv lists as exactly one MANC type.
stimulation: 625 nm, 66 Hz, ~0.040 mW/mm2; 3 s light after 2 s off per trial
frequency_note: Front legs are the main stepping legs across conditions (Fig. 3e)
n_flies_note: 60-70 trials across 6-7 flies per genotype and condition (Fig. 1)
notes: DNg97 alone induces slow forward walking in decapitated flies, with forward velocity measured on the ball (Fig. 1b). I saw no simulation score for DNg97.

title: Central versus peripheral neural control of a coordinated walking pattern in Drosophila
source_locator: bioRxiv v2 Fig. 3g (ball condition), Extended Data Fig. 5
quote: Unilateral DNg100 stimulation drove robust stepping in the ipsilateral front, mid and hind legs across both conditions
mapping_basis: The paper uses the MANC type name DNg100; the driver VT058557;R85F12 is also listed for DNg100 (BDN2) in driver_lines.csv.
stimulation: 625 nm, 66 Hz, ~0.040 mW/mm2; 3 s light after 2 s off per trial
type_coverage: stochastic; unilateral, bilateral and negative classes confirmed by IHC
other_cell_types: non-DNg100 cell types counted per fly in Extended Data Fig. 5 IHC (not named)
coordination_notes: Ipsilateral legs step and contralateral legs show little to no stepping on the ball (one side only).
n_flies_note: N = 92 trials over 10 flies (Extended Data Fig. 5c)
notes: The text says 'leading to turning with low forward and angular velocity'. Rhythm fields are yes because the ipsilateral leg of each pair stepped rhythmically. saw_simulation_score is true for DNg100 (see notes.md).

title: Central versus peripheral neural control of a coordinated walking pattern in Drosophila
quote: front-legs alternation (i1-c1) is only slightly weakened
mapping_basis: The paper uses the MANC type name DNg100, which type_list.csv lists as exactly one MANC type.
stimulation: 625 nm, 66 Hz, ~0.040 mW/mm2; 3 s light after 2 s off per trial
sensory_condition: decapitated, suspended in air, with sets of legs removed (air-stepping)
coordination_notes: Left-right alternation within segments; removing front legs weakens mid-leg (i2-c2) and to some extent hind-leg (i3-c3) coupling.
notes: Leg-removal air-stepping experiment. Coupling of the remaining legs could only be quantified because they stepped rhythmically. behaviour_category forward_walking refers to air-stepping, not locomotion. saw_simulation_score is true for DNg100.

title: Central versus peripheral neural control of a coordinated walking pattern in Drosophila
quote: By titrating optogenetic light intensity, we could get DNg100 stimulated flies to walk slower
mapping_basis: The paper uses the MANC type name DNg100, which type_list.csv lists as exactly one MANC type.
stimulation: 625 nm, 66 Hz; seven intensity levels 0.002 to 0.040 mW/mm2 (strongest 0.040)
frequency_note: Stepping frequency varied with intensity on the ball, less so in air
n_flies_note: each curve one fly; total not read
notes: Strongest-intensity condition recorded. Forward velocity rises with intensity but never exceeds about 8 mm/s. The ball condition for panel a is implied by the forward-velocity measure. saw_simulation_score is true for DNg100.

title: Central versus peripheral neural control of a coordinated walking pattern in Drosophila
source_locator: bioRxiv v2 Extended Data Fig. 7e ('DNg100i (intact flies)')
quote: even if we tested “head-intact” flies or flies with double copy numbers of transgenes
mapping_basis: The paper uses the MANC type name DNg100, which type_list.csv lists as exactly one MANC type.
stimulation: 625 nm, 66 Hz, ~0.040 mW/mm2; 3 s light after 2 s off per trial
sensory_condition: head intact, tethered on air-supported ball
notes: Extended Data Fig. 7e reports forward velocity during activation only; intact DNg100 flies still do not walk faster than about 8 mm/s. The text gives no pre-stimulus or no-light comparison for intact flies, which can walk on their own, so I could not determine a speed change. saw_simulation_score is true for DNg100.

title: Central versus peripheral neural control of a coordinated walking pattern in Drosophila
quote: Co-activating DNg16 with DNg100 did not speed up the velocity or stepping frequencies
mapping_basis: The paper uses the MANC type name DNg100, which type_list.csv lists as exactly one MANC type.
stimulation: 625 nm, 66 Hz, ~0.040 mW/mm2; 3 s light after 2 s off per trial
other_cell_types: ectopic cell types counted in Extended Data Fig. 7d
notes: Co-activation experiment. Relative to pre-stimulus rest, the flies walked forward (decapitated flies do not walk without an effective DN). Relative to DNg100 alone there was no increase in speed (a slight decrease). Coded the same way as sibling record adj-dedicated-0010. saw_simulation_score is true for DNg100.

title: Central versus peripheral neural control of a coordinated walking pattern in Drosophila
quote: Co-activating DNg16 with DNg100 did not speed up the velocity or stepping frequencies
mapping_basis: The paper uses the MANC type name DNg16, which type_list.csv lists as exactly one MANC type.
stimulation: 625 nm, 66 Hz, ~0.040 mW/mm2; 3 s light after 2 s off per trial
other_cell_types: ectopic cell types counted in Extended Data Fig. 7d
notes: Co-activation experiment, coded the same way as sibling record adj-dedicated-0009. The walking comes from co-activation with DNg100. The paper says DNg16 alone 'did not induce any walking in decapitated flies', and adding it did not speed DNg100-driven walking. I saw no simulation score for DNg16.

title: Central versus peripheral neural control of a coordinated walking pattern in Drosophila
quote: both DNg100+DNg75 and DNg100+DNg97 stimulated flies increased stepping frequencies even without the substrate
mapping_basis: The paper uses the MANC type name DNg100, which type_list.csv lists as exactly one MANC type.
stimulation: 625 nm, 66 Hz, ~0.040 mW/mm2; 3 s light after 2 s off per trial
other_cell_types: ectopic cell types counted in Extended Data Fig. 7d
frequency_note: stepping frequency higher than DNg100 alone (Fig. 4g)
notes: Air-stepping without a substrate, so walking speed cannot be measured. The rise in stepping frequency is captured by the leg fields and frequency_note. saw_simulation_score is true for DNg100.

title: Central versus peripheral neural control of a coordinated walking pattern in Drosophila
quote: both DNg100+DNg75 and DNg100+DNg97 stimulated flies increased stepping frequencies even without the substrate
mapping_basis: The paper uses the MANC type name DNg75 (cDN1), which type_list.csv lists as exactly one MANC type.
stimulation: 625 nm, 66 Hz, ~0.040 mW/mm2; 3 s light after 2 s off per trial
other_cell_types: ectopic cell types counted in Extended Data Fig. 7d
frequency_note: stepping frequency higher than DNg100 alone (Fig. 4g)
notes: Air-stepping co-activation with DNg100; walking speed not measurable without a substrate. The paper says DNg75 alone did not induce walking in decapitated flies. I saw no simulation score for DNg75.
